topics.lesson_subject: Residual SQL analytics records after device deletion and controlled cleanup
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Device deletion removes raw log files and archive packets but does not immediately delete already-inserted SQL analytics rows; Log View, FortiView and reports can continue to show historical rows until rebuild or retention cleanup.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Delete authorized device -> remove raw archive artifacts and record local event -> existing analytics database rows remain -> dashboards/reports may still query those rows -> ADOM SQL rebuild or storage-policy retention eventually removes them.
topics.failure_class: Residual analytics evidence after device deletion creates apparent ghost logs or stale report results; premature cleanup risks losing legitimate historical evidence.
topics.evidence_pattern: Device absent from Device Manager while Log View/FortiView still returns its historical records; event log records deletion; ADOM storage info shows Analytics and Archive quotas independently.
topics.remediation_path: Decide whether historical analytics must be retained; rebuild only the affected ADOM when removal is required, or use Keep Logs for Analytics/disk quota/automatic deletion policies with change control and backup.
topics.question_fingerprint: Explain why deleting a device is not equivalent to purging SQL analytics rows and choose the least destructive cleanup method.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Device deletion forks into raw/archive deletion and SQL analytics retention; separate cleanup paths converge at ADOM rebuild or age/quota retention.

topics.lesson_subject: Layer-3 DHCP relay transaction: GIADDR, multiple relay targets and Option 82
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: A FortiSwitch Layer-3 interface relays client DHCP broadcasts to up to eight configured servers, sets GIADDR to identify the client subnet, optionally inserts Option 82, and relays offers back to the client.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Client DHCPDISCOVER broadcast -> relay receives on L3 interface -> GIADDR set to relay address and optional Option 82 added -> copies sent to each relay target -> server selects scope using GIADDR -> DHCPOFFER returns to relay -> relay forwards to client.
topics.failure_class: Wrong DHCP scope, missing relay response, duplicate offers, or Option 82 policy mismatch due to routing, GIADDR, server return route, or relay/Option-82 configuration.
topics.evidence_pattern: Switch relay debug/packet capture shows DISCOVER, GIADDR, Option 82 and each target; server logs show selected scope; offer path confirms return routing. A configured relay IP alone does not prove server reply reachability.
topics.remediation_path: Enable relay on the correct L3 interface, configure up to eight reachable server IPs, decide Option 82 insertion, verify server scope selection and route back to GIADDR; do not enable DHCP server and relay simultaneously on the same interface.
topics.question_fingerprint: Use GIADDR and Option 82 evidence to distinguish wrong scope selection from a missing server return route.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Client VLAN and FortiSwitch L3 SVI in center; relay fan-out to two DHCP servers; response arrows return to SVI then client, with GIADDR and Option 82 labels.
topics.semantic_uniqueness_result: UNIQUE: FortiSwitch L3 DHCP relay is not the FortiGate secondary-IP smart relay or FortiAP per-VAP Option 82 construction covered previously.

topics.lesson_subject: SSID multicast enhancement and IGMP snooping: multicast-to-unicast replication and AP pruning
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiAP maintains IGMP membership per SSID and can translate multicast streams into per-client unicast frames; multicast-enhance is automatically disabled when client count exceeds me-disable-thresh, while IGMP snooping prunes APs without listeners.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Wireless client joins multicast group -> AP observes IGMP membership -> AP/controller updates multicast group membership -> controller forwards only to CAPWAP multicast groups with listeners -> AP optionally replicates multicast payload as per-station unicast until threshold is exceeded.
topics.failure_class: Wireless multicast flooding, missing multicast delivery, excessive airtime consumption, or a sudden behavior change when client count crosses the enhancement threshold.
topics.evidence_pattern: IGMP group table and `diagnose wireless-controller wlac -c vap-mcgrp` show memberships; SSID VAP config shows multicast-enhance, threshold and igmp-snooping; packet capture distinguishes multicast frames from replicated unicast frames.
topics.remediation_path: Enable Advanced Wireless Features, configure per-SSID IGMP snooping and multicast enhancement, set a realistic threshold for client density, verify upstream multicast delivery and client membership; test threshold behavior under expected peak client counts.
topics.question_fingerprint: Distinguish multicast-to-unicast conversion from IGMP pruning and explain why enhancement may stop at the configured client threshold.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Multicast source through controller to two APs; one AP has listeners and replicates to three wireless clients, second AP is pruned; threshold gate shown beside VAP.

topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiNAC schedules archive-and-purge of selected aged log records; archived data can be imported additively, and remote backup retention is separate from local pre-copy backup cleanup.

topics.remediation_path: Verify remote backup target and SSH host key, test the SSH connection, review archive age and schedule cadence together, run controlled Archive/Purge, then confirm success event and archive artifact before assuming live rows were purged.
topics.question_fingerprint: Differentiate archive creation, live-database purge and local-backup cleanup; diagnose an archive/purge failure caused by remote SSH identity change.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiNAC database splits into live eligible rows, archive file destination and remote backup; success gate controls purge; optional import path returns archived rows additively.

topics.lesson_subject: Load-balancing HA synchronization contract: primary-owned objects, replicated authentication data and non-replicated services
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiAuthenticator load-balancing HA uses one standalone primary and up to ten geographically separated load-balancers; only selected authentication configuration categories synchronize, unlike active-passive cluster mode where all configuration synchronizes.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Configure standalone primary and LB nodes -> establish encrypted primary-to-LB synchronization -> choose synchronized setting groups -> LB nodes receive supported users/groups/tokens/certificates/realms/remote servers and selected services -> authentication requests distribute by DNS/NAS/external load balancer.
topics.failure_class: Authentication succeeds on primary but fails or behaves differently on an LB because a required service/object is outside the synchronization contract.
topics.evidence_pattern: Dashboard > HA Status shows synchronization; compare configured service lists and object presence on primary versus LB; LDAP tree/FSSO settings may be absent even while users and groups sync.
topics.remediation_path: Choose active-passive cluster if full configuration replication is required; for load-balancing mode explicitly select supported sync groups and configure non-synchronized features locally or avoid relying on them on LB nodes.
topics.question_fingerprint: Identify which FortiAuthenticator objects synchronize in load-balancing HA and why user replication does not prove LDAP tree/FSSO replication.

topics.lesson_subject: Wildcard remote-user matching under Concurrent Logon licensing and auto-provision precedence
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiPAM 1.9.0 wildcard remote-user entry matches any user authenticated through a selected remote server/group under Concurrent Logon licensing, avoiding one static local mapping per temporary user; auto-provision rules take precedence.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Remote identity authenticates against configured server/group -> wildcard remote-user record matches the remote group -> FortiPAM creates a session with mapped role/privileges -> auto-provision rule precedence is evaluated -> user receives permitted access; notification-dependent roles are not supported for wildcard entries.
topics.failure_class: Remote user authenticates but cannot obtain a FortiPAM session because license model, group match, auto-provision precedence or notification-role constraints are violated.
topics.evidence_pattern: User record shows Match all users in a remote server or group; license is Concurrent Logon; authentication logs show remote group; auto-provision rule and session role show which mapping won.
topics.remediation_path: Use Concurrent Logon licensing, select the correct remote server/group, avoid approval/notification roles on wildcard entries, and test auto-provision precedence with a representative temporary account.
topics.question_fingerprint: Determine when wildcard remote users are valid and why they cannot be assigned notification-generating approval roles.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Remote directory/group -> FortiPAM remote-user wildcard matcher -> auto-provision precedence gate -> FortiPAM session and permitted role; license gate shown before matcher.

topics.lesson_subject: System-owned event timestamps and incident attributes: phRecvTime parser immutability
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiSIEM reserves phRecvTime as the immutable first-received timestamp and prohibits custom parsers from setting it; several event/incident system attributes are also reserved from custom incident-attribute assignment.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Raw event arrives at Collector -> FortiSIEM stamps receive time -> parser extracts vendor/event fields without overriding phRecvTime -> normalized event enters correlation/search -> incident rule action writes only permitted user-defined incident attributes.
topics.failure_class: Parser or rule migration produces invalid/overwritten system metadata, causing misleading ingestion-latency analysis or rule-definition incompatibility.
topics.evidence_pattern: Parser test output shows vendor eventTime separate from system phRecvTime; receive-time delta identifies pipeline latency; rule validation rejects reserved incident fields; raw event and normalized event timestamps can be compared.
topics.remediation_path: Remove phRecvTime from custom parser assignments, preserve source event time in its appropriate event attribute, rewrite user rules to avoid reserved incident attributes, and validate parser/rule changes before upgrade.
topics.question_fingerprint: Explain why parser-supplied phRecvTime is invalid and distinguish source event time from FortiSIEM first-received time.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Raw event with source timestamp enters Collector; FortiSIEM stamps immutable receive time; parser adds vendor fields; correlation engine writes allowed incident attributes while reserved fields remain system-owned.
topics.semantic_uniqueness_result: UNIQUE: prior FortiSIEM lesson covered parser migration, but not the system-owned receive-time/incident-attribute contract introduced in 7.5.x.
